hints: Focus on oxidation numbers, not on the names of the compounds, to see who really gains and loses electrons.
Check magnesium and calcium first, they start as $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ in $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in $\text{CaO}$, now see what they become in $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4$.
Work out silicon in $\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4$ using $\text{Ca}$ as +2 and $\text{O}$ as -2, then compare its start at 0 to its finish to complete the picture.
walkthrough:
**Assign oxidation numbers in the reactants**

Think of oxidation number as the charge an atom would have if we counted electrons. It is the best tool here.

In reactants: $\text{Mg}$ in $\text{MgO}$ is +2, $\text{Ca}$ in $\text{CaO}$ is +2, $\text{O}$ is -2, and free $\text{Si}$ is 0:
$$\text{Mg(+2)O(-2) + Ca(+2)O(-2) + Si(0)}$$

**Assign oxidation numbers in the products**

Now do the same careful counting on the right hand side. Free $\text{Mg}$ is 0.

In $\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4$, $\text{Ca}$ is still +2 and $\text{O}$ is still -2. Let Si be x:
$$2(+2) + x + 4(-2) = 0$$
$$x = +4$$
So we have $\text{Mg(0)}$ and $\text{Ca(+2)}_2\text{Si(+4)O(-2)}_4$.

**Compare changes to find redox**

Reduction is a decrease in oxidation number (gain of electrons). Oxidation is an increase (loss of electrons).

$\text{Mg}$: +2 to 0, decrease, so reduced. $\text{Ca}$: +2 to +2, no change, so neither. $\text{Si}$: 0 to +4, increase, so oxidised.

options.A: Calcium stays as $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in both $\text{CaO}$ and $\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4$, so it is not reduced. Silicon changes from 0 to +4, so it is oxidised, not unchanged.
options.B: Magnesium goes from +2 in $\text{MgO}$ to 0 in $\text{Mg}$, so it gains electrons and is reduced. Calcium stays at +2 throughout, so it is neither oxidised nor reduced.
options.C: It is right that magnesium is reduced (+2 to 0), but silicon is not unchanged. It goes from 0 to +4 in $\text{Ca}_2\text{SiO}_4$, so it is oxidised. This is the trap of forgetting to calculate Si in the silicate.
options.D: Silicon goes from 0 to +4, which is an increase in oxidation number, so it is oxidised, not reduced. Calcium is correctly described as unchanged, but the silicon part makes the whole statement wrong.
